note: IP-neutral (issue #51). Companion droids: three kinds, each with look variants. Not LLM characters; they only beep. The player runs up to max_owned at once. They show in the inventory as droids; what a cargo droid carries does not show, and the Remnant never searches it. Prices: the merchant sells at price and buys back at resale. Looks: each kind's 'look' names its Hyper3D model (issue #25, content/look/gear_models.json), tinted by the variant's body colour ('tint' 0..1), with glowing 'eyes' and a 'muzzle' in model space (metres, facing -Z, standing on y = 0). No model = the droid_kit.gd primitives. Following (issue #25 follow-up): a droid stays put until the player is 'leash' metres away, then walks to its slot and stops within 'settle'.

upgrades.note: The droid merchant's upgrades, per droid (DroidRoster.upgrade). Each has one level per price. health: +per_level of the kind's 'hp' each level (every kind). cargo: +per_level hold slots each level on a droid that carries (a cargo droid starts with its kind's 'cargo_slots'; a slot is one kind of item, any number of it). damage: +per_level of its gun's damage each level (a droid with a gun). Your droids take hits from anyone you are fighting; at 0 hp one is knocked out for knocked_out_s, then reboots at full health.

engage_note: Assassin and floating droids of yours ('engage' on their kind): when one sees an enemy (enemies()) it walks up to 'advance' metres (about ten steps) toward it from where it stood, stopping 'standoff' metres short, and shoots from there. Once that enemy is dead (and no other is in sight) it comes back to you. Walk off far enough and it jumps to you as it always did.

taming.note: Block or deflect this many of the range remote's bolts in a row (a bolt that hits you resets the count) and it follows you home. Oda drops the hint as a rumor (rumors/port_town.json, r_remote_tame).

wrecks.note: Broken droids stranded in the desert. On the home planet's ball the first visit seeds ball_starting_count wrecks across the whole sphere, then every check_seconds of play, with this chance, one more turns up until ball_max_out. They stay at least ball_min_radius from town and ball_min_separation apart along the surface. Flat worlds keep max_out and the ring radii. Fixing one takes fix_seconds; it resets and follows you.

pit_hauler.note: Issue #64: an old cargo droid that rattles round the landing pit, like T-89 a fixture of the pit. Nobody owns it. It carries the pickup named by 'carries' (pickups/port_town.json, pit_jetpack) on its back until someone takes it ([E] beside it, the same pickup as before, so saves still know it is taken). route: pit floor points (town coordinates) it walks in turn, stopping pause_s at each. Oda knows it as a rumor (rumors/port_town.json, r_pit_hauler).

locals.note: Issue #187: the locals' white assassin droids. One walks each outpost the locals hold (its 'patrol' route), and once they hold the barracks two walk the Remnant's old main street patrol (remnant.patrol). They leave you alone until you hurt a local (their side's alarm) or shoot one, then fight like the Remnant's. Not for sale: the merchant's variants are player_variants.

remnant.note: Issue #64/#76: outpost_units are the droids each desert outpost keeps, each walking the outpost's point list named by 'route': an assassin droid on 'patrol', an armed floating droid on 'floater', and a cargo droid on 'cargo' ('walk_speed' sets its own pace). 'flee': when its outpost's alarm goes up (or it is shot) it runs 'distance' metres into the desert, away from you, at 'speed' (giving up after 'max_s'), and is left there broken: a wreck you can fix and keep. A new one turns up at the outpost when the troopers come back. The Remnant's own droids: they patrol the main street ('patrol': out along the street round the north rim of the landing pit and back the same way, never across the pit floor, which is T-89's), share the Remnant's standing (they turn on you when the garrison would), sound the town alarm when they see trouble, and fight. Killing one costs Remnant standing like a trooper.

wreck.note: Issue #148: what is left of the Remnant aboard the crashed starcruiser (src/systems/world/starcruiser_wreck.gd). routes: patrol points in one of the wreck's frames ('level': x, height v, stern-ward w, unpitched; 'hull': the pitched ship's own parts() frame), turned into world points by StarcruiserWreck.site_point. units walk their route and shoot on sight; they answer to no garrison, so nothing out there sounds the town's alarm. A destroyed one comes back on its route after respawn_s. Wreck cleanup: four assassins hold the bridge platform (its landing pad), floating droids drift on every tier, along the gallery and over the hold floor. hauler: an old cargo droid on the starboard deck with the pickup named by 'carries' (pickups/port_town.json, wreck_red_saber) on its back, like the pit hauler.
